policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's 'the way by which thou wentest' addresses the feminine singular addressee and thus distinguishes the qere הָלָכְתְּ ('thou wentest') from ketiv הלכתי ('I went').
ASV explicitly renders 'the days come,' distinguishing the qere בָּאִים ('come/are coming') from the ketiv omission.
ASV explicitly has 'the measuring line,' rendering the qere קָו ('line') and distinguishing it from ketiv קוה.
ASV explicitly renders 'all the fields,' distinguishing the qere הַשְּׁדֵמוֹת ('the fields') from ketiv השרמות.
